bug_semantics: Schema.load(data, many=True) records validation failures by index. For each new invalid item, ErrorStore.store_error wrapped the message as {index: messages} and called merge_errors on the entire accumulated self.errors dictionary; merge_errors copied that growing dictionary before adding the new key. A request with n invalid items therefore copied 0+1+...+(n-1) prior entries, producing quadratic CPU work and disproportionate denial-of-service amplification.
flaw_origin: Commit 8a6ad548df6b9cac377e748551248bde6df5619c changed ErrorStore.store_error in marshmallow/marshalling.py from selecting and updating only the requested index's sub-dictionary to always executing self.errors = merge_errors(self.errors, messages), after wrapping indexed errors in a one-key dictionary. Combined with the already-existing dict(errors1) copy in merge_errors, this is the first commit that rebuilt the complete accumulated indexed-error collection for every item.
ai_marker: absent: the BIC commit object names author Jérôme Lafréchoux <jerome@jolimont.fr> and committer Jérôme Lafréchoux <jlafrechoux@nobatek.com>; its message is only 'Rework Error_store.store_error' and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: GitHub advisory GHSA-428g-f7cq-pgp5 and the published CVE.org record CVE-2025-68480 identify Schema.load(data, many=True) CPU denial of service, affected ranges >=3.0.0rc1,<3.26.2 and >=4.0.0,<4.1.2, and patched releases 3.26.2 and 4.1.2; the CVE state is PUBLISHED and the GHSA withdrawn_at value is null.

git show 8a6ad548df6b9cac377e748551248bde6df5619c -- marshmallow/marshalling.py shows indexed messages newly wrapped as {index: messages} and every error assigned through self.errors = merge_errors(self.errors, messages); the existing merge_errors dict/dict branch copies the complete first argument with errors = dict(errors1).

Direct parent-tree verification at dddaf8edf8dffb0453ac7fb06113f9636985ba90: marshmallow/marshalling.py:36-50 uses get_errors(index), which returns self.errors.setdefault(index, {}), and set_errors(..., index), which assigns only self.errors[index]; the whole-collection merge introduced by the BIC is absent.

git cat-file -p 8a6ad548df6b9cac377e748551248bde6df5619c gives the sole parent dddaf8edf8dffb0453ac7fb06113f9636985ba90, human author/committer Jérôme Lafréchoux, and a message with no trailers or AI marker.
git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms 8a6ad548df6b9cac377e748551248bde6df5619c is contained in tag 3.0.0rc1, matching the first affected boundary.

The advisory-linked merge d24a0c9df061c4daa92f71cf85aca25b83eee508 contains direct 4.x algorithm fix 218d98a785d3bd25dad8880bb07e9cce70340f31 plus tests, defensive input-container copying, and the 4.1.2 version update; its diff changes merge_errors from rebuilding lists/dicts to extending/updating them in place after copying caller-owned message containers.

Release topology checks show 218d98a785d3bd25dad8880bb07e9cce70340f31 is absent from 4.1.1 and present in 4.1.2, while the equivalent 3.x direct fix 0356a3f1c307830f8ded56d823abca5611c594c9 is absent from 3.26.1 and present in 3.26.2.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by the composition of indexed many-item validation with full accumulated-error reconstruction. The earlier b2e5a7da74d2f62a4d3694a43bc31248eb14be24 only introduced merge_errors, and 9a83efdc67b5f694e37d371397b314e6e3fa4dcd still selected the per-index sub-dictionary before merging; neither yet made each indexed failure copy all preceding indices. Commit 8a6ad548df6b9cac377e748551248bde6df5619c is therefore the smallest BIC because it first routed each indexed failure through merge_errors(self.errors, ...), whose dict copy makes total work quadratic. Its immediate parent directly lacks that source-to-sink combination. The fix replaces rebuilding with in-place list/dict merging while first isolating caller-owned containers, and the 3.x/4.x tag checks align with both patched boundaries. The BIC commit object is human-authored and has no AI signal, so this real vulnerability is NOT_AI; later AI-marked repository commits, if any, are irrelevant to BIC attribution.
